title: Census the caller population of the four envelope-returning SDK methods (#13079)
body:
Part of #13079

This PR delivers the census only: it measures the caller population that the card's decision depends on. The convergence itself — option A (converge the four onto `unwrapResponse`) versus option B (keep the envelope and document it) — stays OPEN and remains the maintainer's call on the card, so this must not close it.

## The number

**Zero.** No call site in either reachable repo would break silently if `analytics.query` / `meta` / `explain` and `automation.trigger` started unwrapping.

| population | SDK call sites | would break | how |
|---|---|---|---|
| **objectstack** @ `52bc918e6` (5,527 code files) | 19 | 13 | all **loud**: test assertions and type pins, every one inside `packages/client/src` |
| **objectui** @ `b84dc185` (4,024 code files) | 1 | **0** | the one production site is already shape-tolerant — see below |
| **cloud** | NOT MEASURED | NOT MEASURED | unreachable from this session class |
| published npm consumers | UNMEASURABLE | UNMEASURABLE | outside every repo a sweep can see |

**There are zero production call sites in this repo.** The only non-test occurrence is a docblock.

⛔ **This PR converts nothing.** Zero runtime edits — the convergence is a runtime breaking change to four published methods and is the maintainer's call. The diff is one census test plus the two declarations that test needs.

## The one production call site, and why it survives

`objectui packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts:4846` feeds the resolved value through a chain that already accepts **both** spellings:

```js
const rawRows = Array.isArray(data) ? data
  : data?.rows       && Array.isArray(data.rows)      ? data.rows       // post-unwrap
  : data?.data       && Array.isArray(data.data)      ? data.data
  : data?.data?.rows && Array.isArray(data.data.rows) ? data.data.rows  // envelope, today
  : data?.results    && Array.isArray(data.results)   ? data.results
  : [];
```

Today branch 4 matches; after convergence branch 2 matches. ⚠️ It survives by **defensive coding, not by a designed migration path** — the adapter was written tolerant because the producer was ambiguous. That is the shape a contract-first fix removes rather than leans on, so it should be read as evidence the cost is low, not as evidence the ambiguity is harmless.

## Method, and what a false negative would look like

`tsc` cannot answer this: during the erasure both spellings compiled, so the count comes from reading call sites. A "0 hits" grep is worthless without a positive control, so two failure modes are measured rather than assumed — both pinned as tests:

1. **Comments dominate the raw signal.** A plain `git grep` returns **30** hits here; **10 are docblocks**, not call sites. The census masks comments through `scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs`, the tree's one code/prose separator.
2. ⭐ **A line-based grep under-reports.** `git grep` is line-oriented and this repo contains two `await client.automation` / newline / `.trigger(...)` calls in `client.test.ts`. **A naive sweep misses both** — it reports 17 SDK sites where there are 19. The gap is pinned as a number so a short list cannot read as compliance.

A **false positive** is handled the same way: the bare spelling `analytics.query(...)` also occurs on the real `AnalyticsService`, so every row carries its receiver and that one is classified `NOT_SDK`.

Residual false-negative risk, stated: a call reached through a runtime alias or computed member access (`obj[name](...)`) is invisible to any source scan. Searches for alias capture, destructuring and bracket access found none in either repo.

## The protected counter-example

⛔ `analytics.queryDataset` is **not** a fifth instance. Its route is mounted by `@objectstack/rest` and ends `res.json(result)` with **no envelope to strip**, so it is correct as it stands. It is asserted OUT of the affected set (section 4) because folding it in is the one thing a mechanical sweep gets wrong.

## Two card claims, verified on the tree

- ✅ **`trigger` and `execute` are one door** — with a refinement. They are two *different URLs* (`POST /automation/trigger/:name` and `POST /automation/:name/trigger`), but both resolve to `respondToFlowTrigger` and the same `buildAutomationContext` body translation in `domains/automation.ts`. "Same door" holds at the handler, not at the URL.
- ✅ **The declarations are truthful now.** All four annotations are envelope-shaped, and `return-type-precision.test.ts` pins the payload read as a **`@ts-expect-error`** — the type system does not merely permit the right spelling, it *refuses* the wrong one. Triage's reading that lens ③ no longer favours convergence holds.

## Verification

Union re-run at final commit `097553f19`, after merging `origin/main`.

**Passed — 31 of 35** (`dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, 34 families + `check:nul-bytes`), plus:
- `pnpm lint` — **exit 0**, whole repo, `eslint . --no-inline-config`, no narrowing.
- The census suite — **13 passed (13)**.

**NOT MEASURED — 4, reported separately and never folded into the green list.** All four refuse because this worktree's dependency closure is unbuilt (32 of 68 packages have `dist/`); each names packages this diff never touches, so none is diff-caused:
- `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` — exit 3, "PREREQUISITE NOT MET ... ⛔ This is NOT a pass: nothing was measured."
- `check:type-check-debt` — refuses rather than measure a different world.
- `check:skill-examples` — needs `@objectstack/client-react` built.
- `check:test-completeness` — exit 3, needs a saved test log; its own output says "⛔ It is not a red".

The census file itself typechecks clean: it is **in** `tsconfig.test.json`'s program (confirmed via `--listFiles`) with **0** errors attributed to it.

⚠️ The first derivation named 26 commands; after the diff widened to `turbo.json` and the gate declaration, re-deriving found **8 more families**. Both runs are in the report.

**Reverse verification.** Injected an unclassified call site into `client.test.ts`; mutation confirmed on disk (blob `05154d1d` to `80853cac`), suite went **2 failed / 11 passed** — exactly the two ledger assertions, with all positive controls still green, so the failure was specific and not a harness collapse. Restore proven byte-identical to `HEAD` with `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Known bound

The section-3 ratchet is only as live as turbo's cache: this suite walks the workspace but `@objectstack/client#test` declares its own package plus named cross-package files, so a call site added in **another** package can leave it cached-green. Declaring `packages/**` would re-run the client suite on nearly every commit; recorded as a bound rather than bought at that price. Every site today lives in `packages/client`, where invalidation is normal.

## Changeset

None — test plus build/gate declarations only, publishing nothing from any package. Matches this repo's practice for `test(...)` commits (`978c33f40`, `889ec5b42`, `bcef1cfac` all landed without one). `skip-changeset` applied.
